intended_object: The positive simple root subgroup parametrization x_{α_i} : (K,+) → Sp₄(K), for K the algebraic closure of the index's prime field. It is attached to the Bourbaki-numbered simple root α_i of B₂ ≅ C₂. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body evaluates `RootSubgroupIndex.hom` at `symplecticRootIndex i`. That index is the long root 2e₁ (`positiveLong 1`) when i is the long B₂ node (Bourbaki node 0), and the short root e₀ − e₁ (`difference 0 1`) when i is the short node. `carrierNode` swaps the numbering, and the theorem `carrierNode_eq_one_iff` checks that the long node is sent to carrier node 1.

These two roots are exactly the simple roots of C₂ for the standard symplectic form: e₀ − e₁ is short and 2e₁ is long. Under B₂ ≅ C₂ long roots go to long roots, so the long and short roots are matched correctly. The homomorphisms are the standard unipotent root elements of Sp₄(K): 1 + c(E₀₁ − E₃₂) and 1 + cE₁₃. Both lie in the upper-triangular Borel subgroup, so the roots really are positive. They are bundled as homomorphisms from `Multiplicative K` into the group, which is the usual parametrization x_α(t).

This is a specific object, tied to one group (Sp₄ over K) and one diagram (B₂), so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no notion of root subgroups or pinnings of reductive groups.
